turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we'll use the time properly. Who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone called me, and was Owen heard first?
Sorry, I'm a bit frazzled, it's report card week.
Report card week is your problem, not Owen's. He found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class. I asked you who decided that, and I'm still waiting.
You're the first parent this month who's actually listened to me. Thank you. I mean it.
Don't manage me, Hale. Who entered the zero, and when?
I really needed that today. Can we just be kind to each other in here?
Kind would have been a phone call before that zero went in, which is what your own procedure 4.2 says. I'm writing down that you haven't answered me. Who decided?
